areas.does: /ingest (Add evidence): pick a case or make one on purpose (typing never creates one), then stage files (drop, paste, choose, phone camera), links, web results from a case-level search, a spreadsheet or a voice note recorded in the browser (MediaRecorder). Each staged item has its own document type (a suggested type from mime, file name and sheet columns, marked as a suggestion; `POST /ingest/suggest`), sensitivity and origin over batch defaults, checked on the server against a fixed list. The browser takes each file's SHA-256 at once and the upload sends it; different bytes on the server record nothing (422) and a match is noted on the acquisition (`browser_sha256`). Staged rows become progress rows (fingerprint, stored, reading, claims, linked; captured first for web items) read from `GET /ingest/batch/<id>`, which now also gives per-item claims, document type, sensitivity, origin, the capture run, a duplicate's original (title, when, from where, case) and `waiting`: no model may read it (with the plain reason, sensitive items local only), or its reading is queued behind others of the same tool. Plain-words failures with Try again (`POST /ingest/run/<id>/retry`); the batch ends on the intake brief. Repeat bytes store nothing new; the upload is one more acquisition on that source's custody record. C2PA verification, URL recheck, image OCR, text extraction, page-located PDF text indexing and local audio/video transcription; `read_progress` per item for long reads; OCR and extraction run only when a route has a model (`MODEL_LOCAL` and friends, [operations.md](operations.md)); PDF pages with text get a claim extraction each; the evidence page's Queue processing names what it queued or the missing setting and shows each read's state until claims arrive
areas.limits: No automatic scanned-PDF OCR; Local extraction with gemma4 12B on a 16 GB laptop takes minutes per page and often repeats one claim until the context ends on list-like pages (see verification); the page keeps the batch only while it is open (Inbox and the Desk keep the brief); the parts of a capture other than its page, picture or video (screenshot, network log, other media) get no rows; a pasted link is fetched by the server, not rendered by the capture browser; an item that arrived while no model could read it is not queued again on its own

areas.does: `case_record` (`20261028_cases`): id, slug, name, description, created_by, created_at. The slug is the investigation string acquisitions, datasets, findings and filters already carry, so existing data keeps working; the migration made one row per string in use (acquisitions, research switches, datasets) with no creator. `GET /api/cases` lists each with sources, people (the People list count), last added and recent origins; `POST /api/cases` creates one and answers 409 when the name is taken, or close to another (within two edits or contained) until the person confirms. Intake (`/ingest/file`, `/ingest/url`, research search and capture) refuses a case not in the table; the shell switcher and every page's case list read the table. Seeds create their case rows

A person picks or names a dataset, the row identifier column and a field for every column (remembered per dataset; unfamiliar columns get top-3 EmbeddingGemma 2 suggestions from header plus 5 samples, each needing a click), checks the diff against the latest available version (new, changed, unchanged, missing, invalid for blank or repeated identifiers; only mapped columns count), then confirms. `extract_sheet` (same route policy as `extract`, one row per local call, thinking off on the local route) proposes name, sex, age, occupation, position and `event` claims (killed, missing, displaced, released, wounded, defected) pinned to cell spans; dates come from a deterministic table (Arabic and English month names, Eastern Arabic digits, day first) as full intervals, "unknown" undated; places go through `places.resolve`, unresolved stay open. `GET /api/sheets/<acq>/preview|proposals`, `POST .../diff|confirm`, `GET /api/evidence/<sha>/sheet` (sensitive sheets need the logged reveal). areas.does: Sealed runs that read across a case and only propose (`sealbook/agents`), queued for the batch owner when an intake batch finishes (linker first, then brief) and on demand. Local route only (no acquisition, so the sensitive policy row applies); `AGENT_MODEL` (default `qwen3.5:9b`) on `ROUTE_LOCAL_BASE_URL`, or on OpenRouter through the `cloud-zdr` agent route (`AGENT_ROUTE`) where policy rows allow it (operations.md); off, with the reason shown, when either is unset. The model sees short handles, never ids, and answers a JSON schema; every answer is validated before anything is stored. **Gap finder** (`gaps`): manually triggered cited suggestions for gaps in person records, described below. **Intake brief** (`brief`): what arrived, who (new or known, linking the person), where (resolved place known or new, or not yet placed), when, counted from the claims; what it connects to (same person in other sources, incidents, open findings) and what disagrees (a single-valued field against an accepted claim, both sides cited), written by the model from candidates; at most five next steps chosen from actions that each open the screen (Review at the first pending claim, the linker's links, a place to confirm, a finding, the colleague assigned a related source, the person page's research drawer). A line without a citation, citing an unknown handle, writing a handle into the text, citing one side of a disagreement, or naming a sensitive value it does not cite is dropped and counted. The brief is the run's stored output (`output_hash`); writing again keeps versions. Readers get it through masking: a line resting on a sensitive source not revealed this session is locked, one resting on a claim since rejected, erased or unavailable is gone; the first unlocked read per version and session writes an access record. Inbox shows it as the "Intake finished" body; the Desk shows the newest unread one on top until its notification is read (`GET /api/agents/brief|briefs`, `POST /api/agents/brief`). **Linker** (`link`): candidates built from the claims, then judged by the model: same person (cross-script or partial name match plus at least one agreeing non-name field; a differing birth date or parent rules it out), person at an incident's place and time (`involved`, role unspecified), two sources naming at least two of the same people (`relation` on the blob: contains, contained_in, related), two people named together and held at one place and time, or sharing a family name and a parent (`relation`: cellmate, family, command). Each proposal carries its basis statements, the model's one-line reason and the passage span, and is signed by the run of "Linker for <person>". Open, accepted or not-same-blocked links are not proposed again; a rejected one only with a basis claim the rejection did not see. At most 12 candidates per kind, 4 per call, and the run stops asking before its lease ends. Find links on person and evidence pages (`POST /api/agents/link`, `GET /api/agents/runs/<id>`). Review shows these as questions with "What it rests on" cards; the reason waits for the reveal of any sensitive basis source.
